fix_draft.title: Self-employed pension contributions are ~3% of SOI Keogh payments (max $1,771/person)
fix_draft.body: The retirement_contributions stage (us/spec/sources.yaml:458-530) allocates ASEC RETCB_VAL and QRF-imputes it onto the PUF half, so PUF tax-form Keogh/SEP/SIMPLE deduction amounts never reach self_employed_pension_contributions_desired. Released populace-us-2024-spm-20260915: $1.37B on 5.4M persons (max $1,771) vs IRS SOI TY2023 Table 1.4 'Payments to a Keogh plan' $30.13B on 946K returns ($24.3B at AGI $200K+). The JCT Keogh calibration target sits at -98.8% and cannot move under max_weight_ratio 5. Proposed: source the PUF half from the PUF Keogh-deduction field (verify field ID against the PUF codebook) and/or add SOI Table 1.4 Keogh returns/amount targets. Keep the JCT row as a broad-fit anchor only: JCX-48-24 measures a net exclusion of contributions and earnings.

fix_draft.body: On populace-us-2024-spm-20260915 at policyengine-us 2.2.1, filers with AGI $1-1.5M = 1.20M (SOI TY2023 369K), $1.5-2M = 326K (147K), $5-10M = 12K (49K), $10M+ ~0 (30K); total $1M+ AGI matches SOI ($2.61T vs $2.54T). AMT ($4.39B vs SOI $2.75B) comes from 70 records, 43 of them at $1-2M AGI with weights 10-30K. The only $1M+ AGI-class targets (TY2022 taxable interest) miss by +65% (returns) and -39% (amount). Proposed: add SOI Table 1.4 AGI-class return counts and AGI amounts for the $500K+ classes; investigate why the Forbes-backed top tail gets ~zero weight; optionally add SOI AMT returns/amount. Annotation for the scorecard: AMT is a top-tail statistic resting on 70 records and has moved $1.1B-$4.4B across releases.
